name: Fjøset
description:
History

Fjøset is one of the original buildings of the Ella Ø Station [235] originating from the Lauge Koch Expeditions 1931-58.  The house was used as canteen, kitchen, and storage for the expeditions. Later on Fjøset for many years was used by the Sirius Patrol as carpenter workshop and for storage purposes. In 2021 Sirius decided to abandon Fjøset and build a new carpenter workshop on the military area at Ella Ø station, leaving Fjøset to Nordøstgrønlandsk Kompagni Nanok (Nanok) for renovation, use and administration. In the summer of 2022 Nanok - sponsored by Aage V. Jensens Fonde - has undertaken a complete renovation and refitting of Fjøset. The house has four rooms. Three with bunk beds.

Important notices 

Access to all parts of the Ella Ø Station requires permission from the military authorities (Joint Arctic Command).

The Greenland government authorities has granted Nanok a land allocation (arealtildeling) to a specific area  (see image) of the Ella Ø station, including the houses: Ørnereden, Fjøset, and Tolvmandsbarakken. The area is named "Nordøstgrønlandsk Kompagni Nanok Station Ella Ø". Nanok is therefore permitted to organize and administer this area. The remaining part of the Ella Ø station is administered by the military authorities. As a consequence no equipment, material, provisions, cargo, containers, etc. should be moved to - or left in - this area without prior permission. In the Nanok allocated area there is also a scientific monitoring station with sensitive measuring equipment. Helicopter operations will therefore not be allowed in the area. 

Use and access 

Fjøset (and Tolvmandsbarakken) serves as Nanok's base camp in the Ella Ø region. The house is well suited for housing for 4 up to max. 6 persons. One of the two larger rooms is suited for meeting or dining purposes for up to 15 persons. The other large room is intented to be used as a electronics or fine-mechanics workshop for preparing / repairing scientific equipment. The two smaller rooms are always reserved to Nanok, whenever a Nanok crew is present at Ella Ø.

Fjøset is usually locked to the public. It is available only to Nanok and to scientific non-profit activities, and only after prior agreement with Nanok. In case anyone want to use Fjøset for accomodation, they must remove all used and unused leftovers and equipment before departure at the end of the stay. Applications are prioritized as follows:

  1. Nanok
  2. Scientific non-profit expeditions/projects

In order to get access to Fjøset users must sign an agreement with Nanok. There will be a fee pr. day pr. person for use of Fjøset. Scientific expeditions: Start fee DKK 2,000.00 per person, thereafter DKK 700.00 per person per day. You may contact Nanok (e-mail: nanok@xsirius.dk) for further information. 

The house must always be left only in a good condition, meaning:

  • Any damages repaired
  • Door locked and windows / shutters securely closed.
  • Hut nicely swept and cleaned
  • Hut lamps filled and the glass removed
  • Matchboxes with matches ready in opening
  • Snow shovel secured and visible on the outside of the house
  • No garbage or any kind of food in or near the house
  • Electrical and gas appliances, and water supply disabled and secured for winter.
  • Note: Due to possible damage by polar bears the present condition of the house is not known

..................................................................................................................................................

For further use and access information, please contact Nordøstgrønlandsk Kompagni Nanok.

Aage V. Jensens Fonde sponsor Nanok's work.

Numbers in brackets [ ] refer to hut number in P.S. Mikkelsen: "North-East Greenland 1908-60.  The Trapper Era"  (2008) published by Scott Polar Research Institute.
